source_text: I. Imperatore Valeriano quartum et Gallieno tertium consulibus, tertio kalendarum Septembrium, Carthagine in secretario Paternus proconsul Cypriano episcopo dixit: Sacratissimi imperatores Valerianus et Gallienus litteras ad me dare dignati sunt, quibus praeceperunt eos qui Romanam religionem non colunt, debere Romanas caeremonias recognoscere. exquisivi ergo de nomine tuo, quid mihi respondes? Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Christianus sum et episcopus. nullos alios deos novi nisi unum et verum deum, qui fecit caelum et terram, mare et quae sunt in eis omnia. huic deo nos Christiani deservimus, hunc deprecamur diebus ac noctibus pro nobis et pro omnibus hominibus et pro incolumitate ipsorum imperatorum. Paternus proconsul dixit: In hac ergo voluntate perseveras? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Bona voluntas, quae deum novit, immutari non potest. Paternus proconsul dixit: Poteris ergo secundum praeceptum Valeriani et Gallieni exsul ad urbem Curubitanam proficisci? Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Proficiscor.
thought_title: Cyprian confesses he is a Christian bishop and accepts exile
orientation: At Carthage the governor Paternus questions Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, about the emperors order to perform Roman worship.
pass_a_gloss: When the emperor Valerian was consul for the fourth time and Gallienus for the third time, on the third day before the Kalends of September, at Carthage in the council chamber, Paternus the governor said to Cyprian the bishop: The most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus have deigned to give a letter to me, by which they have ordered that those who do not cultivate the Roman religion ought to recognize the Roman worship rites. I have inquired therefore concerning your name: what do you answer to me? Cyprian the bishop said: I am a Christian and a bishop. I know no other gods except the one and true God, who made heaven and earth, sea and all things which are in them. To this God we Christians do service, him we entreat by days and by nights on behalf of ourselves and on behalf of all men and on behalf of the safety of the emperors themselves. Paternus the governor said: Do you therefore persist in this resolve? Cyprian the bishop answered: A good resolve, which has come to know God, cannot be changed. Paternus the governor said: Will you therefore be able, according to the order of Valerian and Gallienus, to set out as an exile to the city of Curubis? Cyprian the bishop said: I am setting out.

pass_b_english: In the fourth consulship of Valerian and the third of Gallienus, three days before the Kalends of September, at Carthage in the council chamber, Paternus the governor spoke to Cyprian the bishop: "The most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus have seen fit to send me a letter, commanding that those who do not practice the Roman religion must perform the Roman worship rites. I have asked about your identity, so what do you answer?"

Cyprian the bishop said: "I am a Christian and a bishop. I know no other gods but the one true God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them. We Christians serve this God, and we pray to him day and night for ourselves and for all people and for the safety of the emperors themselves."
Paternus the governor said: "Do you stand firm in this resolve then?" Cyprian the bishop replied: "A good resolve that knows God cannot be changed."
Paternus the governor said: "Then will you go into exile to the city of Curubis, as Valerian and Gallienus command?" Cyprian the bishop said: "I will go."
